      Now I understand the structure. The Go server on port 8080 serves the

<html>
  <head>
    
  </head>
  <body>
    <p style="margin-top: 0px">
      I created a multi-stage <code>Dockerfile</code> and a <code>.dockerignore</code> 
      that build and run both the frontend and backend.
    </p>
    <p>
      <strong>Dockerfile</strong> (3 stages):
    </p>
    <ol>
      <li>
        <strong>frontend-builder</strong> (<code>node:22-alpine</code>) &#8212; 
        installs npm dependencies and runs <code>npm run build</code> to 
        produce the Vite/React static files in <code>frontend/dist</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>backend-builder</strong> (<code>golang:1.27-alpine</code>) &#8212; 
        downloads modules and compiles a static Go binary (<code>CGO_ENABLED=0</code>).
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>runtime</strong> (<code>alpine:3.20</code>) &#8212; a minimal final 
        image that copies the Go binary and the built <code>frontend/dist</code>, 
        preserving the relative path layout the server expects. Exposes port <code>8080</code> 
        and runs the binary.
      </li>
    </ol>
    <p>
      <strong>Key detail:</strong> <code>server.go</code> serves static files 
      from the relative path <code>frontend/dist</code>, so the runtime stage 
      keeps that exact <code>frontend/dist</code> structure under <code>/app</code> 
      and sets <code>WORKDIR /app</code> so the path resolves correctly.
    </p>
    <p>
      To build and run:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="860,955" data-copilot-content-offset="874,952" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="powershell"><code>docker build -t sezzle-calculator .
docker run -p 8080:8080 sezzle-calculator</code></pre>
    <p>
      Then open <a href="http://localhost:8080/">http://localhost:8080/</a>.
    </p>
    <p>
      A couple of notes:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        The Dockerfile references <code>go.sum</code> and <code>package-lock.json</code> 
        optionally (<code>go.sum*</code> / <code>package-lock.json*</code>) 
        since neither is currently in the repo. If you add them later, they'll 
        be picked up automatically for better caching. Without a lockfile, <code>npm 
        install</code> is used instead of <code>npm ci</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        If you don't have Docker installed locally I couldn't verify the 
        build; let me know if you'd like me to run it.
      </li>
    </ul>
  </body>
</html>
